operations.old: [F5] If $M$ has bracket $\int\sigma\sigma^{\mathsf T}dt$ and $\sigma^{-1}$ is bounded, the inverse-diffusion integral is Brownian by the proved local representation lemma. [[lem-elliptic-local-martingale-brownian-representation]]
operations.new:
[F5] For a predictable invertible matrix process $\sigma$ with bounded inverse and finite pathwise squared energy, bracket $\int\sigma\sigma^{\mathsf T}dt$ yields a Brownian inverse-diffusion integral and the recovery identity $M=\int\sigma\,dB$, without continuity of $\sigma$. [[lem-predictable-elliptic-martingale-brownian-reconstruction]]

[F6] The predictable sigma-algebra contains deterministic Borel time functions and adapted left-step processes; limits and Borel compositions of predictable maps are predictable. [[def-progressively-measurable-and-predictable-process]]

operations.old: 4.1 Put $\sigma_r=\sigma_{T-r}(Y_r)$. Uniform nonsingularity gives a bounded inverse, and [F5] constructs $B_u=\int_0^u\sigma_r^{-1}dM_r$ with bracket $uI_d$. AC and the vector Lévy characterization in [F5] make $B$ standard Brownian in the reversed filtration. Using $dM_u=\sigma_{T-u}(Y_u)dB_u$ in the drift decomposition proves that $Y$ is a weak solution of the displayed reverse SDE. The assumed well-posedness and nonexplosion of the reverse martingale problem identify its law uniquely and complete the theorem. [F5, A1, step 3.2] ∎
operations.new: 4.1 To handle the Borel coefficients allowed by the SDE data, choose the predictable representative $\widehat Y$ obtained as follows: take left-step approximations with coefficients $Y_{kT/2^n}$, set their time-zero value to $Y_0$, and take their pointwise limit where finite and $0$ otherwise. These maps are predictable by [F6] and agree with $Y$ at every time on its common continuity event. The pair $(r,\widehat Y_r)$ is predictable, so the joint Borel coefficient gives a predictable matrix $\Sigma_r=\sigma_{T-r}(\widehat Y_r)$; inversion is Borel on invertible matrices, and $\|\Sigma_r^{-1}\|$ is uniformly bounded. Step 3.2 gives $\int_0^T\|\Sigma_r\|_F^2dr=\operatorname{tr}[M]_T<\infty$ almost surely, as well as $[M]_u=\int_0^u\Sigma_r\Sigma_r^{\mathsf T}dr$. Thus [F5] constructs $B=\int\Sigma^{-1}dM$ Brownian in the original reversed filtration, and proves $M=\int\Sigma\,dB$. Since $\widehat Y=Y$ on a common full event, this is the displayed reverse SDE with its original Borel coefficient. The assumed well-posedness and nonexplosion of the reverse martingale problem identify its law uniquely and complete the theorem. [F5, F6, A1, step 3.2] ∎

operations.old: [[thm-markov-diffusion-reversal-by-bayes-kernels|The positive-density Bayes-kernel reversal theorem]] supplies the reverse drift under the uniform nonsingularity, forward-equation, integrability, and reverse martingale-problem hypotheses restated above.
operations.new:
[[thm-markov-diffusion-reversal-by-bayes-kernels|The positive-density Bayes-kernel reversal theorem]] is applied with horizon $S=T-\epsilon$ to $\overline X_r=X_{\epsilon+r}$, $0\le r\le S$, on the shifted filtration $\overline{\mathcal F}_r=\mathcal F_{\epsilon+r}$ and with Brownian motion $\overline W_r=W_{\epsilon+r}-W_\epsilon$. Brownian increments remain independent of $\overline{\mathcal F}_r$ by the original increment hypothesis, and the shifted filtration retains the usual conditions. The shifted coefficients are $\overline b_r(x)=b_{\epsilon+r}(x)$ and $\overline\sigma_r(x)=\sigma_{\epsilon+r}(x)$; changing variables in the Lebesgue and elementary stochastic integrals, then passing to their localized limits, gives $d\overline X_r=\overline b_r(\overline X_r)dr+\overline\sigma_r(\overline X_r)d\overline W_r$. Its marginal densities are $\overline p_r=p_{\epsilon+r}$ and its transition densities are $\overline q(r,x;s,y)=q(\epsilon+r,x;\epsilon+s,y)$. Positivity, normalization, Markov identities, forward equations, uniform nonsingularity, integrability, and the assumed reverse martingale problem transfer by this deterministic time translation. Its reverse process is $\overline X_{S-u}=X_{T-u}$ with natural reversed filtration $\mathcal G_u=\sigma(X_{T-v}:0\le v\le u)$, and its Bayes kernels become
$$\overline K_{u,v}(y,dx)=\frac{p_{T-v}(x)q(T-v,x;T-u,y)}{p_{T-u}(y)}dx,\qquad0\le u<v\le S.$$
The supplier therefore gives precisely the displayed reverse coefficients and a Brownian driver in this reversed filtration, retaining Borel time dependence of $\sigma$.
